answer.rationale: Primary contract lapses in 14 days with no auto-renew while the line sits at 94% with no buffer, so delivery continuity dominates. Deferral is a poor fit: c5 applied to a non-critical renewal that continued month-to-month, which this contract is not known to allow. Switching primary (c2) or standing up a second source (c3) would spend the single decision on a change that can raise onboarding or split-volume risk and still leave the expiring primary unsettled. c1 supports staying on the incumbent to avoid integration and delivery interruption. c4 and c6 (the records being verified) indicate that renewal-window benchmarking and a longer commitment have previously moved incumbent price and terms without shrinking scope—the path most aligned with an 18% spend cut that does not increase delivery risk. Unverified whether an 18% reduction is actually achievable or whether a multi-year lock-in is compatible with a one-year mandate.
